subject: No-training confirmation & backup retention edge cases
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: written confirmation on training + backup/snapshot retention

Hi Mina,

Hope you're well. As part of our procurement checklist, our security team needs a written confirmation that Redwood will not use FintechCo customer content to train language models or otherwise derive training signals. This is separate from telemetry/metrics — they want an explicit assurance about model training.

A couple of follow-ups they care about:
- Are backups/snapshots ever used for training? If snapshots are replicated for DR, do they enter any training pipelines?
- Retention nuances: we want to understand the TTL for snapshots, nightly backups, and long-term archives — especially where those artifacts live and which tenants (if any) are co-located.
- Deletion playbook: when data deletion is requested for a tenant, how are backups and snapshots handled (e.g., tombstoned, purged, re-encrypted)? What is the expected timeline and proof we can receive?

If you can provide an attestation or pointer to a signed doc and an operational summary (short bulleted timeline + any edge-case exceptions), that would help unblock legal/vendor review.

Thanks — we need this by EOD Wednesday so procurement can move to redlines next week.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Security Operations, FintechCo
[attachment: vendor-questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: written confirmation on training + backup/snapshot retention

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer content (including backups/snapshots of customer workloads) to train or fine-tune our models. I will attach our standard signed attestation and a retention matrix for the artifacts you referenced.

Operational summary (high level):
- Training: Customer payloads (API requests, files, embeddings, etc.) are excluded from model training pipelines by policy and by technical controls. We separate telemetry/metrics (aggregated, non-PII) used for product quality from any training data.
- Backups & snapshots: Snapshots created for DR are encrypted and retained according to a tiered schedule; they are not piped into training. If a snapshot is restored for debugging or customer-requested recovery, the payload remains isolated; no automated ingestion into trainer systems occurs.
- Deletion playbook: On delete requests we tombstone tenant metadata and schedule secure purge of backups/snapshots within the stated windows. Short-lived caches are wiped immediately; nightly backups are rotated out according to retention tiers (see matrix).

I am attaching two artifacts now: our non-training attestation (signed PDF) and a snapshot-retention matrix that lists TTLs by artifact type, replication region, and expected purge windows.

Marissa & Ben — can you confirm the timeline wording for edge-case restores and whether there are circumstances (legal hold, e-discovery) that can extend retention? I want to make sure we capture exceptions for FintechCo's legal team.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_no_training_attestation.pdf]
[attachment: snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: written confirmation on training + backup/snapshot retention

Mina — quick clarifications for the attestation wording and the matrix so legal has no surprises:

1) Restores & debugging: restorations are performed into isolated tenant environments; engineering may create ephemeral diagnostic copies but those are logged and are excluded from any automatic training ingestion. If an engineer needs to use any restored content in a retraining experiment (extremely rare), that would require a documented approval chain and customer consent. We should state that in the attestation as an explicit exception.

2) Replica artifacts in partner regions: where snapshots are replicated to partner-managed storage (e.g., cloud-object-replica), retention follows the partner contract. We should call out that customer can request evidence of deletion from partner storage and that Redwood will coordinate.

3) Legal holds: put a short line that legal holds can supersede standard purge windows; in those cases, Redwood will notify the customer about extended retention and provide scope.

I've annotated the matrix with suggested TTL clarifications and added a column for "exception conditions." Marissa — I've left two cells for your input on SLA timelines for purge proofs.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: written confirmation on training + backup/snapshot retention

Mina / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — they look good. A few action items before we can close:
- Can you include the small clause Ben suggested about the rare, documented case where restored content could be used for retraining and that such use requires explicit customer consent? FintechCo Legal wants that in plain language.
- We need a signed attestation file (PDF) with the exception language included and the signature block for Redwood's Head of Trust & Safety. PDF we received appears unsigned; could you provide the signed copy and an internal point of contact for attestation verification?
- For evidence of purge/proof, can Redwood provide an audit record (timestamped event id + operator id) that we can reference in case of dispute? If not, please outline the alternative proof (e.g., storage lifecycle logs + S3 object deletions + KMS key rotation entries).

If you can get the signed attestation and an updated matrix with the three clarifications by EOD Monday, we can move forward with finalizing procurement. Appreciated.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Security Operations, FintechCo
